name: tool-approval
purpose: A user-authorized action in a conversation (Cloudscape user-authorized actions, AI Elements Confirmation): the agent proposes something with consequences — call a tool, run a command, deploy, delete — and the reader approves or denies it before anything runs. The card states the action as a question (``Allow `npm test`?``), says what will happen, shows exactly what will run in its body (a `CodeBlock` with the command, `KeyValueList` with parameters), and offers Deny and Approve. Once decided, the buttons give way to the outcome in text (`Approved`, `Denied`, `Request expired`) so the decision stays in the thread. Irreversible actions (`variant="danger"`) turn Approve destructive and can require typing a phrase first. With `editable` (opt-in) the reader corrects the call's arguments in a code field before approving; the edit comes back through `v-model` and `approve`. It is a card in the conversation, not a dialog: it does not trap focus and does not take initial focus; `focus()` moves focus to its heading when the owner wants to bring the reader to it.
useWhen: Use ToolApproval only inside an AI conversation when an agent asks permission to run a tool or command; for a person confirming an action they started use ConfirmDialog.
One-time authorization of a consequential action proposed by an agent: a production deployment, a purge, a command.
Arguments the reader may want to correct first (a URL list, a limit): add `editable`.
avoidWhen: Tools already trusted for the session → record the call with `tool-call`, do not ask again.
A destructive action the reader started themselves in the UI → `confirm-dialog`.
A form → this card only approves or denies.
related: `tool-call` — the record of the call after it is approved (or `denied`).
`confirm-dialog` — confirmation of the reader's own destructive action.
`code-block`, `key-value-list` — what will run, in the body.
`chat-message` — the assistant acknowledges the decision in the next message.
bestPractices: Title is a question naming the action and target; put tool and command names in backticks (code).
Match the approve label to the title verb (`Deploy`, `Delete`) when it is not a generic tool call.
Never pre-focus or pre-select Approve for a risky action.
Do not leave a request pending forever: expire it (`status="expired"`) and have the assistant say nothing ran.
After Deny, the assistant acknowledges in the conversation ("Skipping that step.").
With `editable`, bind `v-model` to the arguments as formatted JSON, set `invalid` while they do not parse, and run the call with the `input` that `approve` carries.
Keep `editable` off for irreversible actions unless the edit is the point: the phrase confirms the target, the edit can change it.

props.name: title
props.doc: The question, naming the action: ``Allow `npm test`?``, `Approve deployment to production?`. Backticks render as code.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences on what will happen and to what; backticks render as code.

props.name: status
props.doc: `pending` asks; `approved`, `denied` and `expired` replace the buttons with the outcome in text.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `danger` for an action that cannot be undone: the approve button turns destructive.

props.name: confirmationPhrase
props.doc: A word the reader must type before Approve enables, for irreversible actions (the resource name). Empty asks for no typing.

props.name: approveLabel
props.doc: Text of the approve button, the verb of the title (`Deploy`, `Delete`). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Approve`).

props.name: denyLabel
props.doc: Text of the deny button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deny`).

props.name: loading
props.doc: A decision is being sent; both buttons are inert and Approve shows its loading state.

props.name: editable
props.doc: Lets the reader edit the call's input in a code field before approving; the edit comes back through `v-model` and `approve`.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: The edited input cannot be used (it does not parse): the field shows an error and Approve stays disabled. Has no effect without `editable`.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: What exactly will run: a `CodeBlock`, or `KeyValueList` with parameters.
